_doc: Personnel the GFP totals do not break down. ground_share: share of active personnel in ground combat forces (army, marines/naval infantry, airborne, ground special forces), used to count infantry; countries not listed use default_ground_share, the median of those that are. organised_reserve: reservists trained and assigned to wartime units, callable within weeks (not paper reserve totals); a nation fighting for survival calls them up over mobilisation_days (default_mobilisation_days when no source states it; never fewer than MIN_MOBILISATION_DAYS in conflict/land_warfare.py). Every entry keeps the totals it was derived from, its sources and the fields its researcher flagged as uncertain. Researched from search-result snippets quoting the IISS Military Balance (mostly via the Norwegian encyclopedia snl.no) and official national figures.

ARM.notes: Active 44,800: Army 41,850 (0.93), Air/AD aviation 1,100, other AD 1,850. IISS reserve 210,000 (served within 15 yrs; organisation unclear) -> organised null.

AUS.notes: Active 59,800: Army 29,400 (0.49), Navy 15,500, RAAF 14,900. IISS reserve 29,750 (active reserve) used as organised_reserve (flag).

AZE.year: IISS Military Balance 2024/2025 total; Army figure from MB2019
AZE.notes: Active 64,050; Army 56,850 (MB2019 when total was 66,950) -> 0.89 (0.85 on MB2019 totals). IISS reserve 300,000 (ex-conscripts). Some sources (GFP-type) give 126,400 active. No sourced organised-reserve figure.

BLR.year: IISS Military Balance 2025 total; branch split from other sources
BLR.notes: IISS 2025: 48,600 active (other count 45,350). Ground = Ground Forces ~18,000 (2024) + Special Operations Forces ~6,150 (MB2022) = 24,150 -> 0.50 ESTIMATE (mixed sources). IISS reserve 289,500 (served within last 5 years). Territorial-defence/people's-militia plans are paper -> organised null.

BRA.notes: Active 366,500: Army 214,000 (112,000 conscripts) + Marines 16,000 = 230,000 (0.63); Navy 85,000 incl. marines, AF 67,500. IISS reserve 1,340,000 (paper).

CAN.notes: Active 66,500: Army 22,500 (0.34), Navy 12,600, RCAF 12,100, remainder joint/SOF/support. IISS reserve 34,400 (Primary Reserve, unit-based part-timers) used as organised_reserve (flag).

CHE.year: IISS Military Balance 2023 (via SNL); Swiss Army headcount Mar 2024
CHE.notes: IISS 'active' 19,550 (16,450 conscripts in training) is a joint figure with no army/air split -> ground_share null (land component clearly dominant; air force militia squadrons stood down). Militia army headcount ~147,000 (1 Mar 2024; regulated strength 100,000, legal ceiling 140,000) = organised_reserve. IISS reserve 123,450. WEA reform: 35,000 troops deployable within 10 days -> mobilisation_days 10 (for that first echelon).

CHN.year: IISS Military Balance 2023-2025 (figures unchanged across editions)
CHN.notes: PLA active 2,035,000; Ground Force ~965,000 + PLAN Marine Corps ~35,000 (SNL citing IISS; other estimates 30-40k, some 2026 claims ~100k) = 1,000,000 (0.49). Navy ~260,000, Air Force ~395,000, Rocket Force/support the rest. Reserve 510,000 (IISS) is organised in PLA reserve divisions/brigades, so used as organised_reserve (flag). PAP 500,000 paramilitary excluded; militia (millions, paper) excluded.

DEU.notes: 182,857 soldiers (Jan 2025; 184,194 Dec 2025). Heer 62,108 (0.34); Luftwaffe 27,642, Marine 15,549, Joint Support 23,520, Medical 20,372, CIR etc. Army includes KSK/airborne. Active (assigned) reservists ~34,000; IISS reserve ~34,600. Plan: 260,000 active + 200,000 reserve by mid-2030s.

EGY.notes: Active 438,500: Army 310,000 (incl. ~200,000 conscripts) (0.71); Air Defence Command, AF 30,000, Navy 18,500. IISS reserve 479,000 (ex-conscripts; organisation unknown) -> organised null.

ERI.notes: Active 201,750, mostly indefinite national-service conscripts: Army ~200,000 (0.99). IISS reserve ~120,000 (est.). In Sept 2022 all reservists up to age 55 were recalled (coercive round-ups) -- no sourced organised figure or timeline.

ESP.notes: Active 124,150: Army 71,900 + Marines 5,350 = 77,250 (0.62); Navy 20,500, AF 20,350. IISS reserve 14,700 (voluntary reservists).

EST.year: Estonian Defence Forces / MoD 2023-2025 (IISS breakdown not retrieved)
EST.notes: Active 8,200 incl. ~4,000 conscripts. Ground ~6,000 = average peacetime size of the Land Forces (soldiers, conscripts, officers) -> 0.73 ESTIMATE. Wartime structure 43,700: 4,200 active/permanent-readiness + 38,800 reservists and Defence League members with wartime posts (= organised_reserve); ~40,000 more trained but unassigned; ~230,000 in mobilisation register; plan to raise wartime structure to ~50,000. National Defence Act allows call-up on 24 h notice; President: mobilisation 'in a matter of hours and days' -> mobilisation_days 1 (flag).

ETH.notes: Active ~503,000 after wartime expansion: Army ~500,000, AF 3,000 (0.99). Pre-2020 IISS figure was ~138,000. Regional special forces/militias (e.g. Amhara Fano, regional police) excluded. No reserve figure.

FIN.year: IISS Military Balance (~2022/2023 edition, via Forces News); wartime strength from Finnish govt
FIN.notes: IISS: 19,250 active (Army 13,400, Navy 3,150, AF 2,700) -> 0.70. SNL (peacetime staff + annual conscripts): Army 4,400+~18,000, Navy 1,400+3,200, AF ~2,000+1,300 -> ~0.74. Wikipedia: ~24,000 active incl. conscripts. Wartime strength 280,000 (Army wartime ~180,000); organised_reserve = 280,000 - ~24,000 active = 256,000 (derived). IISS reserve 238,000 (= previous wartime strength); total trained reservists ~870,000-900,000. Rapid call-up of up to 25,000 reservists without 3 months' notice since 2016; no sourced overall mobilisation time.

FRA.year: IISS Military Balance 2023/2024 (via SNL); operational reserve Oct 2025
FRA.notes: Active 203,250: Army 114,800 + naval commandos/fusiliers ~2,200 = 117,000 (0.58); AF 40,200, Navy 34,850. Gendarmerie 100,500 excluded. organised_reserve = operational reservists ~48,600 (31 Oct 2025; target 80,000 by 2030). IISS reserve 36,300.

GBR.year: UK MoD Quarterly Service Personnel Statistics, 1 Jan 2026 (Full-Time Trained Strength)
GBR.notes: Full-time trained strength: Army 70,630, RN/RM 28,140, RAF 27,670 = 126,440 (UK Regulars incl. untrained 136,960). Ground = Army 70,630 + Royal Marines ~6,500 (2021 figure, RM not published separately) = 77,130 -> 0.61. organised_reserve = trained Future Reserves 2020 ~29,060 (Army Reserve 23,740). Earlier IISS (via Forces News) 153,200 active (Army 85,800) -> 0.56.

GRC.notes: Active 132,200: Army 93,500 (45,000 conscripts) (0.71); Navy 16,700, AF 21,800. IISS reserve 289,000; reservists are pre-assigned to units by the Army mobilisation directorate. 2025 MoD plan for 150,000 'combat-ready' Army reservists (not yet achieved -> organised null). The 1996 Imia mobilisation was completed within a single day -> mobilisation_days 1 (historical, flag).

IND.notes: Active 1,475,750: Army 1,237,000 + navy marine commandos ~1,200 = 1,238,200 (0.84); Navy 75,500, AF 149,900, Coast Guard 13,350. IISS reserve 1,155,000 (Army 960,000 ex-regulars liable to recall; not formed units). organised_reserve = Territorial Army 'over 40,000' (other reports ~50,000); 14 TA infantry battalions were activated in May 2025.

IRN.notes: Active 610,000: Artesh Ground Force 350,000 (220,000 conscripts) + IRGC Ground Forces ~150,000 = 500,000 (0.82); Artesh Navy 18,000, AF 37,000, AD 15,000; IRGC total 190,000 (navy ~20-25k, aerospace ~15k). IISS reserve 350,000. Basij: ~600,000 said to be mobilisable (SNL), poorly trained paramilitary -> not counted as organised reserve (null).

IRQ.notes: Active 193,000: Army ~180,000 (0.93). Paramilitary ~86,000 (incl. Federal Police ~36,000); Popular Mobilisation militias ~180,000 'available on mobilisation' (paramilitary, not an organised military reserve) -> null.

ISR.notes: IISS: 169,500 active, Army 126,000 (0.74). IISS reserve 465,000 (all assigned to reserve units). organised_reserve = demonstrated call-up of ~360,000 in Oct 2023 (IDF: 300,000 within 48 h) -> mobilisation_days 2. Use 465,000 as the theoretical ceiling.

ITA.notes: Active 161,050: Army 93,100 + San Marco marines ~3,000 = 96,100 (0.60); Navy 28,700, AF 39,250. Carabinieri ~108,000 excluded. IISS reserve 17,900 (Army 13,400); no separate organised-reserve figure found.

JPN.year: IISS Military Balance 2023/2024 (via SNL); MOD actual reserve fill (latest MOD page)
JPN.notes: IISS: 247,150 active, GSDF 150,700 (0.61). These are close to AUTHORISED strength; actual SDF manning ~227,843 (92%, FY2023). organised_reserve = actual Ready Reserve 3,805 + Reserve SDF personnel 32,267 = 36,072 (MOD; authorised 7,981 / 47,900). IISS reserve 55,900.

KOR.notes: MB2023: 555,000 active; Army 420,000 + Marines 29,000 = 449,000 (0.81). Actual strength has fallen to ~450,000 (2025) and the plan figure is 500,000 (Army 365,000, Marines 29,000 -> 0.79) -- share is stable ~0.8. Reserve: IISS 3,100,000 (total incl. homeland reserve). organised_reserve = mobilisation reserve (dongwon yebigun, 1-3/4 yrs after discharge, assigned to wartime mobilisation divisions/units): ~1.3M, being cut to ~950,000 under Defense Reform 2.0 (Aju News 2020); total reserve ~2.56-2.75M, ~1.7M trained annually but only 2-3 days/yr. No sourced mobilisation timeline.

LTU.year: IISS (via SNL/Wikipedia, ~2021-2023 data); Lithuanian MoD plans
LTU.notes: 23,000 active. Land Forces ~12,000 active + ~3,500 conscripts = 15,500 -> 0.67 ESTIMATE (excludes ~5,500 NDVF volunteers, which IISS counts as paramilitary militia). organised_reserve = 'active reserve' (ex-conscripts within 10 yrs, trained, equipped, assigned to units): 28,000 (2021); other reports 36,000-38,000; plan 50,000 by 2030. IISS reserve 7,100.

LVA.year: SNL 2026 / Latvian MoD-LSM 2024-2025 (IISS breakdown not retrieved)
LVA.notes: ~8,000 active (professional + National Defence Service conscripts). Navy ~500 and Air Force ~250 (SNL) -> everything else (land forces, SOF, staff/logistics) 7,250 = 0.91 UPPER BOUND; true combat-ground share lower. National Guard (Zemessardze) ~10,000 volunteers + ~12,000 designated reserve soldiers -> organised_reserve ~22,000 (ESTIMATE); further ~26,000 older trained reservists. Target 61,000 total (31,000 active incl. NG/high-readiness reserve) by ~2030-36.

NLD.notes: Military personnel 44,245 (1 Sep 2025; appears to include Royal Marechaussee and central staff). Army 17,806 active + Korps Mariniers ~2,300 = 20,106 -> 0.45. Using IISS definitions (2018: 35,400 total excl. Marechaussee; Army 18,850 + marines 2,650) the share is 0.61 -- choose 0.45 if the sim's total includes all uniformed personnel. Reservists 8,510.

NOR.year: IISS Military Balance (~2022 edition, via Forces News); MB2024 total 25,400
NOR.notes: IISS: 23,950 active: Army 9,350 (0.39), Navy 4,300, AF 3,600 (rest joint/HV staff). MB2024 total 25,400 (branch split not retrieved). Home Guard ~40,000-40,500 (IISS lists 40,000), incl. ~3,000 high-readiness 'innsatsstyrker'. Total strength on full mobilisation ~70,000 (Wikipedia). organised_reserve = Home Guard 40,000.

PAK.notes: Active 660,000: Army 560,000 + Marines 3,200 = 563,200 (0.85); Navy 30,000, AF 70,000. IISS lists no formal reserve figure we could confirm; Wikipedia/GFP-type sources give 550,000 'reserve' (ex-servicemen, not organised) -> null. Paramilitary (FC, Rangers ~290k) excluded.

PHL.notes: Active 145,300: Army 103,200 + Marines 8,300 = 111,500 (0.77); Navy 24,500 incl. marines, AF 17,600. IISS reserve 131,000; CAFGU militia ~50,000 (paramilitary).

POL.year: Polish MoD 2024 total; branch split via SNL (approximate)
POL.notes: Total 216,100 (2024; >220,000 by Aug 2026). Ground = Army ~110,000 + Special Forces ~5,000 + Territorial Defence ~40,000 (SNL) = 155,000 -> 0.72 ESTIMATE. Caution: 2025 budget data for PROFESSIONAL soldiers only list Land Forces 71,714, Air 21,980, Navy 8,240, WOT 5,850 (rest in central/joint units) which would give a lower share (~0.55-0.6). Wartime: >550,000 incl. >300,000 reservists could be mobilised (Polish Radio) -> organised_reserve 300,000 is a PLAN figure; active reserve/high-readiness reserve still being built (target 150,000 by 2039).

PRK.year: IISS Military Balance (2020-2025 editions, unchanged); ROK Defense White Paper agrees
PRK.notes: Active 1,280,000: Army ~1,100,000 (0.86), Navy 60,000, Air Force 110,000, Strategic Forces ~10,000. IISS reserve 600,000 = Reserve Military Training Units (organised, used as organised_reserve, flag). Worker-Peasant Red Guards ~5.7M and Red Youth Guard ~1M are paramilitary militia, excluded. ROK DWP gives ~7.6M total reserve incl. militia.

ROU.notes: Active 71,500: Army 35,500 (0.50), Navy 6,800, AF 11,700, remainder joint/SOF/other. Gendarmerie 57,000 excluded. IISS reserve 55,000; reserve ageing (avg age ~48-50); 2025 law creates 4-month voluntary training feeding an operational reserve (size not yet reported).

SAU.notes: Active 257,000: Army 75,000 + National Guard 130,000 (mechanised/infantry brigades, ground combat) + Marines 3,000 = 208,000 (0.81); AF 20,000, Air Defence 16,000, Navy 13,500 (incl. marines), Strategic Missile Force. No reserve listed.

SGP.year: IISS Military Balance 2023/2024 (via SNL); MINDEF mobilisation exercises
SGP.notes: Active 51,000: Army 40,000 (26,000 conscripts) (0.78); AF 6,000, Navy 4,000. IISS reserve 252,500 = operationally ready NSmen assigned to units -> organised_reserve. MINDEF open-mobilisation drills: >90% of activated NSmen report within a few hours; units equipped same day -> mobilisation_days 1 (actually <1).

SRB.notes: Active 28,150: Army 13,250 (0.47; includes river flotilla), Air Force & AD 5,100, rest training/joint commands. IISS reserve 50,150; 'active reserve' ~2,000; passive reserve ~600,000 (paper).

SWE.year: IISS Military Balance 2024; wartime organisation per Swedish govt/Armed Forces 2024-25
SWE.notes: MB2024: 14,850 active: Army 6,850 (0.46), Navy 2,350 (incl. amphibious corps, not separable), AF 2,700, other 2,950. Wartime organisation ~88,000 (to 115,000 by 2030, ~130,000 by 2035). organised_reserve = 88,000 - 14,850 = 73,150 (derived; includes Home Guard ~22,000 and conscript-trained reservists with wartime placements). IISS reserve 11,450. Home Guard readiness '6-24-90' (start tasks in 6 h, full capability 24 h) -> mobilisation_days 1 applies to Home Guard.

SYR.year: 2026 (post-Assad new Syrian Army); pre-fall IISS MB2023 given in notes
SYR.notes: Assad-era SAA dissolved Dec 2024. New army reported at ~180,000-182,000 after SDF integration (Aug 2026), target 300,000; division counts are considered inflated. Air force/navy largely destroyed (Dec 2024 strikes) so the force is overwhelmingly ground: ground_share 0.95 is an ESTIMATE, not sourced. Pre-fall IISS MB2023: 169,000 active, Army 130,000 (0.77), AF 15,000, AD 20,000; paramilitary ~100,000. No organised reserve.

TUR.notes: Active 355,200: Army 260,200 + Marines 3,000 = 263,200 (0.74); Navy 45,000 incl. marines, AF 50,000. IISS reserve 378,700. Gendarmerie (~150k+) excluded (NATO counts give ~494,500 incl. gendarmerie).

TWN.notes: Active 169,000: Army 94,000 + Marines 10,000 (in Navy 40,000) = 104,000 (0.62); AF 35,000. IISS reserve 1,657,000 is a paper figure. Legislative Yuan (Jun 2024): 1,981,822 listed reservists, 710,569 within 8 yrs (trainable), only ~110,000 trained in 2024; Tung Hsin mobilisation drill 2024 used 14,647. organised_reserve = MND's first-response plan: 450,000 force incl. ~260,000 reservists + ~185,000 standing (Minister Yen De-fa via Taipei Times). MND mobilisation office claims 215,000 reservists can be mobilised within 24 h (+78,000 standby) -> mobilisation_days 1 is an OFFICIAL CLAIM; readiness of those units is widely doubted (reserve brigades formed in 18 counties; 14-day refresher every ~2 yrs).

USA.year: FY2025 authorised end strength (DoD request via CRS IN12447); DMDC actual 1,285,084 on 30 Sep 2025
USA.notes: Active: Army 442,300 + USMC 172,300 = 614,600 of 1,276,700 (Navy 332,300, USAF 320,000, USSF 9,800) -> 0.48. organised_reserve = Selected Reserve 765,700 (ARNG 325,000, USAR 175,800, USNR 57,700, USMCR 32,500, USAFR 67,000, ANG 107,700); ground subset ARNG+USAR+USMCR = 533,300. All are drilling unit members, but Guard/Reserve combat brigades need weeks-months of post-mobilisation training (no sourced figure) -> mobilisation_days null. IISS reserve not retrieved.

VEN.notes: Active 123,000: Army 63,000 + Naval Infantry ~15,000 = 78,000 (0.63); Navy 25,500 incl. marines, AF 11,500, National Guard 23,000 (gendarmerie; counting it as ground gives 0.82). IISS reserve 8,000. organised_reserve = Bolivarian Militia ~220,000 'armed and ideologically close' (IISS paramilitary estimate; 343,000 in 2020) -- low military value, flag. Government claims 4.5M+ militia (not credible).

VNM.notes: Active 482,000: Army 412,000 + Naval Infantry ~27,000 = 439,000 (0.91); Navy 40,000 incl. NI, Air Defence/AF 30,000. Reserve commonly cited (IISS) ~5,000,000 (SNL wording suggests 500,000 militia reservists -- conflicting, flag). Self-defence militia excluded.
uncertain_fields: naval infantry 27k looks high vs other estimates

RUS.notes: Total 900,000 (IISS, 2021) per EUAA citing Military Balance. Ground = Ground Forces 280,000 + VDV 45,000 + naval infantry 35,000 = 360,000 (SOF/Spetsnaz brigades are GRU and largely inside Ground Forces figure). Reserve: official/IISS 'reserve' ~2,000,000 on paper (MB2023 lists 1,500,000); RAND (2019) judged only 4-5k were an active reserve in the Western sense; BARS contract reserve grew 'from a few thousand to ~100,000' in 2021 (Meduza via Moscow Times) -> organised_reserve 100,000 is an UPPER-BOUND claim. Mobilisation: Sept-2022 'partial mobilisation' of 300,000 (mostly NOT pre-assigned organised reservists) was declared complete in ~37 days (21 Sep-28 Oct 2022); only 82,000 were in the zone at completion, 41,000 in combat units -> mobilisation_days=37 describes that call-up, not an organised-reserve readiness standard.

UKR.year: IISS Military Balance 2022 (data as of late 2021)
UKR.notes: MB2022: active 196,600; land forces 125,600; Air Assault Forces ~20,000 (Feb 2022) -> ground 145,600 (0.74). Two naval-infantry brigades (35th, 36th) sit inside the Navy total and are NOT added (no sourced personnel figure); adding a few thousand would raise the share to ~0.76. MB2021 (data 2020) gave 209,000 active incl. army ~145,000. Reserve: IISS 900,000 (mostly 2014-21 combat veterans). organised_reserve = ~234,000 discharged servicemen enrolled in the 'military-operational reserve' (May 2021, MoD/ArmyInform) assigned to replenish units; +~11,000 reserve-contract personnel; TDF reserve >200,000 claimed by Reznikov. Observed: 37,000 reservists joined TDF by 26 Feb 2022; armed forces reached ~700,000 by July 2022 (~4.5 months). No sourced single 'days' figure.

RUS.year: IISS Military Balance 2025 (data as of early 2025; MB2026 Russia branch figures not found)
RUS.notes: MB2025: total ~1,134,000; Ground Forces ~550,000, VDV 35,000, naval infantry 10,000 (heavy losses) -> ground 595,000 (52.5%). MB2025 also records ~617,000 personnel deployed to/near Ukraine (Dec 2024) and ~20,000 PMC. MB2023 (via SNL) gave 1,190,000 with Army 550,000 (incl. ~300k mobilised), VDV 40,000, NI 30,000 -> 0.52, consistent. Authorised strength: Sept-2024 decree 1.5M servicemen; March-2026 decree 2,391,770 total incl. 1,502,640 servicemen (actual strength lower). Wartime replacement is by contract recruitment (~30,000/month in Q2 2026; ~172-200k in H1 2026), not an organised reserve; reserve size is secret (official claims ~2M 'active reserve' in 2025, ICDS researcher suggests <1M). 2026 law lets reservists be called for 'special training' to guard infrastructure. organised_reserve left null.
uncertain_fields: ground_share (Russian ground strength includes mobilised + contract fillers; NI/VDV heavily attrited)

UKR.year: IISS Military Balance 2025 branch breakdown (as reported by Slovo i Dilo / Dupuy Institute)
UKR.notes: MB2025 armed-forces branches: Ground Forces ~500,000, Territorial Defence ~100,000, Air Assault ~45,000, Navy ~40,000 (incl. ~30,000 marines), Air Force ~35,000, SOF ~5,000, Unmanned Systems ~5,000 => sum 730,000. Ground = 500k+100k+45k+30k marines+5k SOF = 680,000 (0.93). Plus ~260,000 in National Guard/Border Guard etc. (MB2025 overall ~990,000). Zelensky: 880,000 (Jan 2025); SNL: >900,000 at end-2025 with land forces ~600,000; MB2026 ~880,000 (fakty.com.ua). Apply the 0.93 share to whichever total the sim uses (National Guard combat brigades are also ground forces). No organised reserve: replacement via general mobilisation at ~30,000/month (Zelensky/Syrskyi 2024-25).
uncertain_fields: total_active (730k armed forces vs 880k-990k incl. NGU/DPSU)
